chapterTitle: Introduction
title: Title and extent of operation of the Code
summary: The Code is named here, and this section says where it applies.

chapterTitle: Introduction
title: Punishment of offences committed within India
summary: People in India can be punished under the Code for acts or failures to act that break its rules.

chapterTitle: Introduction
title: Punishment of offences committed beyond, but which by law may be tried within, India
summary: The Code can apply to acts abroad when Indian law allows a trial in India.

chapterTitle: Introduction
title: Extension of Code to extra-territorial offences
summary: The Code also covers certain crimes committed outside India.

chapterTitle: Introduction
title: Certain laws not to be affected by this Act
summary: This Code does not replace certain other laws.

chapterTitle: General Explanations
title: Definitions in the Code to be understood subject to exceptions
summary: The Code definitions and crime rules must be read with the exceptions set out in the Code.

chapterTitle: General Explanations
title: Sense of expression once explained
summary: A term defined in the Code keeps that meaning wherever it is used.

chapterTitle: General Explanations
title: Gender
summary: Words for one gender can refer to any gender, unless the context shows otherwise.

chapterTitle: General Explanations
title: Number
summary: A word in the singular can also mean the plural, and the other way around.

chapterTitle: General Explanations
title: “Man”, “Woman”
summary: Explains how the Code uses the words man and woman.

chapterTitle: General Explanations
title: “Person”
summary: In the Code, a person can be an individual or an organization.

chapterTitle: General Explanations
title: “Public”
summary: Explains what public means in the Code.

chapterTitle: General Explanations
title: Definition of “Queen”
summary: This section once defined “Queen”. The source marks it omitted.

chapterTitle: General Explanations
title: “Servant of Government”
summary: A servant of Government means a person employed or paid by the Government.

chapterTitle: General Explanations
title: Definition of “British India”
summary: This section once defined “British India”. The source marks it repealed.

chapterTitle: General Explanations
title: Definition of “Government of India”
summary: This section once defined “Government of India”. The source marks it repealed.

chapterTitle: General Explanations
title: “Government”
summary: Explains what Government means in the Code.

chapterTitle: General Explanations
title: “India”
summary: Explains what India means in the Code.

chapterTitle: General Explanations
title: “Judge”
summary: Explains who counts as a judge under the Code.

chapterTitle: General Explanations
title: “Court of Justice”
summary: Explains what counts as a court of justice.

chapterTitle: General Explanations
title: “Public servant”
summary: In this Code, a public servant is a person who holds or performs a public office or duty.

chapterTitle: General Explanations
title: “Movable property”
summary: Explains what counts as movable property; land and things fixed to it are excluded.

chapterTitle: General Explanations
title: “Wrongful gain”
summary: unlawful gain means getting property unlawfully; unlawful loss means someone unlawfully losing property.

chapterTitle: General Explanations
title: “Dishonestly”
summary: A person acts dishonestly when they intend to cause unlawful gain or unlawful loss.

chapterTitle: General Explanations
title: “Fraudulently”
summary: A person acts fraudulently when they act with intent to defraud.

chapterTitle: General Explanations
title: “Reason to believe”
summary: A person has reason to believe something when there is enough cause to believe it.

chapterTitle: General Explanations
title: Property in possession of wife, clerk or servant
summary: Property held by a wife, clerk, or servant for someone else is treated as being in that other person's possession.

chapterTitle: General Explanations
title: “Counterfeit”
summary: Counterfeiting means making one thing resemble another to deceive or assist deception.

chapterTitle: General Explanations
title: “Document”
summary: A document is recorded information that can be used as evidence.

chapterTitle: General Explanations
title: “Electronic record”
summary: An electronic record has the meaning given to it by the information-technology law.

chapterTitle: General Explanations
title: “Valuable security”
summary: A valuable security (a document affecting legal rights) is a document that creates, changes, transfers, or ends a legal right or duty.

chapterTitle: General Explanations
title: “A will”
summary: A will is a document meant to take effect after its maker dies.

chapterTitle: General Explanations
title: Words referring to acts include illegal omissions
summary: References to acts can also include failures to do something required by law.

chapterTitle: General Explanations
title: “Act”, “Omission”
summary: Explains how the Code uses the words act and omission (a failure to act).

chapterTitle: General Explanations
title: Acts done by several persons in furtherance of common intention
summary: When people act together with a shared purpose, each may be responsible for the shared act.

chapterTitle: General Explanations
title: When such an act is criminal by reason of its being done with a criminal knowledge or intention
summary: When a crime depends on a particular intention or knowledge, people acting together with that same intention or knowledge may each be responsible.

chapterTitle: General Explanations
title: Effect caused partly by act and partly by omission
summary: A result can be caused by an act, a failure to act, or both.

chapterTitle: General Explanations
title: Co-operation by doing one of several acts constituting an offence
summary: A person who deliberately helps carry out a crime by doing one of its component acts may be treated as a participant.

chapterTitle: General Explanations
title: Persons concerned in criminal act may be guilty of different offences
summary: People involved in the same act may be responsible for different crimes, depending on their own conduct and state of mind.

chapterTitle: General Explanations
title: “Voluntarily”
summary: deliberately or knowing the result was likely (intentionally or knowing the result was likely) means intending a result, or knowing or having reason to believe it is likely to happen.

chapterTitle: General Explanations
title: “Offence”
summary: In some sections, the word offence also includes certain punishable acts under other laws.

chapterTitle: General Explanations
title: “Special law”
summary: A special law applies to a particular subject.

chapterTitle: General Explanations
title: “Local law”
summary: A local law applies only in a particular part of the country.

chapterTitle: General Explanations
title: “Illegal”, “Legally bound to do”
summary: Illegal includes conduct that is a crime, forbidden by law, or grounds for a civil claim. A person is legally bound to do something if failing to do it is illegal.

chapterTitle: General Explanations
title: “Injury”
summary: Injury includes unlawful harm to a person's body, mind, reputation, or property.

chapterTitle: General Explanations
title: “Life”
summary: Life means human life, unless the context indicates otherwise.

chapterTitle: General Explanations
title: “Death”
summary: Death means the death of a human being, unless the context indicates otherwise.

chapterTitle: General Explanations
title: “Animal”
summary: Animal means any living creature other than a human being.

chapterTitle: General Explanations
title: “Vessel”
summary: A vessel is anything made to carry people or property by water.

chapterTitle: General Explanations
title: “Year”, “Month”
summary: Year and month are counted by the British calendar.

chapterTitle: General Explanations
title: “Section”
summary: A section is a numbered part of a chapter in the Code.

chapterTitle: General Explanations
title: “Oath”
summary: Oath includes a legally accepted affirmation or declaration.

chapterTitle: General Explanations
title: “Good faith”
summary: good faith (with due care and attention) requires due care and attention.

chapterTitle: General Explanations
title: “Harbour”
summary: Harbouring includes sheltering, supplying, or otherwise helping someone evade arrest, subject to the stated exceptions.

chapterTitle: Of Punishments
title: Punishments
summary: Lists the punishments available under the Code.

chapterTitle: Of Punishments
title: Construction of reference to transportation
summary: References to transportation in other laws are generally read as references to imprisonment for life or treated as omitted, depending on the wording.

chapterTitle: Of Punishments
title: Commutation of sentence of death
summary: The appropriate Government may replace a death sentence with another punishment under the Code, without the person's consent.

chapterTitle: Of Punishments
title: Commutation of sentence of imprisonment for life
summary: The appropriate Government may replace a life sentence with imprisonment for a term of up to fourteen years.

chapterTitle: Of Punishments
title: Definition of “appropriate Government”
summary: Explains whether the Central or State Government is the appropriate Government for sections 54 and 55.

chapterTitle: Of Punishments
title: Sentence of Europeans and Americans to penal servitude. Proviso as to sentence for term exceeding ten years but not for life
summary: This repealed section set out when Europeans and Americans could receive imprisonment with hard labour, including terms over ten years but not life.

chapterTitle: Of Punishments
title: Fractions of terms of punishment
summary: For calculating fractions of a sentence, life imprisonment is counted as twenty years.

chapterTitle: Of Punishments
title: Offenders sentenced to transportation how dealt with until transported
summary: This repealed section covered offenders sentenced to transportation how dealt with until transported. The source marks it repealed.

chapterTitle: Of Punishments
title: Transportation instead of imprisonment
summary: This section was repealed and no longer sets out a rule.

chapterTitle: Of Punishments
title: Sentence may be (in certain cases of imprisonment) wholly or partly rigorous or simple
summary: When either kind of imprisonment is allowed, the court may choose rigorous imprisonment (with hard labour), simple imprisonment, or a mix.

chapterTitle: Of Punishments
title: Sentence of forfeiture of property
summary: This repealed section covered sentence of forfeiture of property. The source marks it repealed.

chapterTitle: Of Punishments
title: Forfeiture of property, in respect of offenders punishable with death, transportation or imprisonment
summary: This repealed section allowed property to be taken for certain serious crimes. The source marks it repealed.

chapterTitle: Of Punishments
title: Amount of fine
summary: If a law sets no maximum fine, the court may set any amount, but it must not be excessive.

chapterTitle: Of Punishments
title: Sentence of imprisonment for non-payment of fine
summary: A court may order imprisonment if a fine is not paid, in addition to any other sentence.

chapterTitle: Of Punishments
title: Limit to imprisonment for non-payment of fine, when imprisonment and fine awardable
summary: For crimes punishable by both prison and a fine, the extra prison term for not paying the fine is limited.

chapterTitle: Of Punishments
title: Description of imprisonment for non-payment of fine
summary: The extra imprisonment for not paying a fine may be of a kind allowed for the crime.

chapterTitle: Of Punishments
title: Imprisonment for non-payment of fine, when offence punishable with fine only
summary: If a crime is punishable only by a fine, unpaid fines can lead only to simple imprisonment, subject to the stated limits.

chapterTitle: Of Punishments
title: Imprisonment to terminate on payment of fine
summary: Imprisonment imposed for not paying a fine ends when the fine is paid or collected.

chapterTitle: Of Punishments
title: Termination of imprisonment on payment of proportional part of fine
summary: Paying part of a fine can shorten the extra prison term in proportion to the amount paid.

chapterTitle: Of Punishments
title: Fine leviable within six years, or during imprisonment — Death not to discharge property from liability
summary: A fine can generally be collected within six years, or before a longer prison term ends. The offender's death does not release property that remains legally liable for the debt.

chapterTitle: Of Punishments
title: Limit of punishment of offence made up of several offences
summary: A person should not receive multiple or excessive punishments for one crime made up of overlapping crimes, unless the law expressly allows it.

chapterTitle: Of Punishments
title: Punishment of person guilty of one of several offences, the judgment stating that it is doubtful of which
summary: If the court is unsure which of several crimes was committed, it must impose the least severe available punishment.

chapterTitle: Of Punishments
title: Solitary confinement
summary: A court may order a person serving rigorous imprisonment to spend limited periods alone, subject to strict time limits.

chapterTitle: Of Punishments
title: Limit of solitary confinement
summary: Limits how long solitary confinement (being kept alone) may last at one time and requires breaks between periods.

chapterTitle: Of Punishments
title: Enhanced punishment for certain offences under Chapter XII or Chapter XVII after previous conviction
summary: A person previously convicted of certain theft- or property-related crimes may face a higher penalty for another such conviction.

chapterTitle: General Exceptions
title: Act done by a person bound, or by mistake of fact believing himself bound, by law
summary: A person is not committing a crime when the law requires the act, or when an honest factual mistake makes them believe it is required.

chapterTitle: General Exceptions
title: Act of Judge when acting judicially
summary: A judge is not committing a crime when acting judicially within legal authority.

chapterTitle: General Exceptions
title: Act done pursuant to the judgment or order of Court
summary: An act carried out in good faith (with due care and attention) under a court order is not a crime while the order remains in force.

chapterTitle: General Exceptions
title: Act done by a person justified, or by mistake of fact believing himself justified, by law
summary: A person is not committing a crime when the law justifies the act, or an honest factual mistake makes them believe it is justified.

chapterTitle: General Exceptions
title: Accident in doing a lawful act
summary: An accidental result is excused when it happens during a lawful act done lawfully and with proper care.

chapterTitle: General Exceptions
title: Act likely to cause harm, but done without criminal intent, and to prevent other harm
summary: An act likely to cause harm may be excused when done in good faith (with due care and attention) to prevent a greater harm, without criminal intent.

chapterTitle: General Exceptions
title: Act of a child under seven years of age
summary: A child under seven cannot commit a crime under the Code.

chapterTitle: General Exceptions
title: Act of a child above seven and under twelve of immature understanding
summary: A child aged seven to under twelve is excused if they lack enough understanding to judge the act and its consequences.

chapterTitle: General Exceptions
title: Act of a person of unsound mind
summary: A person is excused if a serious mental condition made them unable to understand the act or that it was wrong or unlawful.

chapterTitle: General Exceptions
title: Act of a person incapable of judgment by reason of intoxication caused against his will
summary: A person is excused for an act done while unable to understand it because someone intoxicated them without their knowledge or against their will.

chapterTitle: General Exceptions
title: Offence requiring a particular intent or knowledge committed by one who is intoxicated
summary: Voluntary intoxication does not usually remove the knowledge required for a crime; the rule differs when the intoxicant was given without the person's knowledge or against their will.

chapterTitle: General Exceptions
title: Act not intended and not known to be likely to cause death or grievous hurt, done by consent
summary: Consent can excuse harm only where death or serious injury was neither intended nor known to be likely, and the consenting person is an adult.

chapterTitle: General Exceptions
title: Act not intended to cause death, done by consent in good faith for person’s benefit
summary: A good-faith act for someone's benefit may be excused if they consent, provided the act is not intended to cause death.

chapterTitle: General Exceptions
title: Act done in good faith for benefit of child or insane person, by or by consent of guardian
summary: A guardian may consent to certain good-faith acts for a child or person unable to make decisions, but the Code sets strict limits on death and serious injury.

chapterTitle: General Exceptions
title: Consent known to be given under fear or misconception
summary: Consent is invalid if it results from fear or a serious misunderstanding, or if the person cannot understand the choice. A child under twelve generally cannot give consent for this purpose.

chapterTitle: General Exceptions
title: Exclusion of acts which are offences independently of harm caused
summary: Consent does not excuse an act that is a crime regardless of whether it harms the person who agreed.

chapterTitle: General Exceptions
title: Act done in good faith for benefit of a person without consent
summary: A good-faith act for someone's benefit may be excused without consent when consent cannot be obtained in time, subject to limits including those on causing death or injury.

chapterTitle: General Exceptions
title: Communication made in good faith
summary: A good-faith message for someone's benefit is not a crime merely because it harms them.

chapterTitle: General Exceptions
title: Act to which a person is compelled by threats
summary: A person forced by a threat of immediate death may be excused, except for murder and certain crimes against the State.

chapterTitle: General Exceptions
title: Act causing slight harm
summary: A harm so slight that an ordinary person would not complain is not a crime.

chapterTitle: General Exceptions
title: Things done in private defence
summary: An act done to defend a person or property is not a crime when it falls within the right of private defence.

chapterTitle: General Exceptions
title: Right of private defence of the body and of property
summary: A person may defend their own or another's body, and their own or another's property, within the Code's limits.

chapterTitle: General Exceptions
title: Right of private defence against the act of a person of unsound mind, etc
summary: A person may defend against an act even when the actor is excused because of age, mental condition, intoxication, or mistake.

chapterTitle: General Exceptions
title: Acts against which there is no right of private defence
summary: Private defence has limits: it cannot be used against certain good-faith official acts, when authorities can provide protection in time, or to cause more harm than necessary.

chapterTitle: General Exceptions
title: When the right of private defence of the body extends to causing death
summary: In listed serious attacks, including attacks involving likely death, rape, kidnapping, or acid, private defence of the body may extend to causing death.

chapterTitle: General Exceptions
title: When such right extends to causing any harm other than death
summary: In other attacks, private defence of the body may cause harm but not death.

chapterTitle: General Exceptions
title: Commencement and continuance of the right of private defence of the body
summary: The right to defend the body starts when a reasonable threat arises and lasts while the danger continues.

chapterTitle: General Exceptions
title: When the right of private defence of property extends to causing death
summary: Private defence of property may extend to causing death only for listed serious crimes, including robbery and nighttime breaking into a building.

chapterTitle: General Exceptions
title: When such right extends to causing any harm other than death
summary: For other theft, property damage, or trespass, private defence may cause harm but not death.

chapterTitle: General Exceptions
title: Commencement and continuance of the right of private defence of property
summary: Explains when the right to defend property starts and how long it lasts for different crimes.

chapterTitle: General Exceptions
title: Right of private defence against deadly assault when there is risk of harm to innocent person
summary: A person defending against a deadly attack may risk accidentally harming an innocent person if there is no effective alternative.

chapterTitle: Of Abetment
title: Abetment of a thing
summary: A person helps commit a crime by encouraging it, joining a qualifying plan, or intentionally assisting it.

chapterTitle: Of Abetment
title: Abettor
summary: An abettor is a person who encourages or helps a crime, even if the person they help cannot themselves be held responsible for it.

chapterTitle: Of Abetment
title: Abetment in India of offences outside India
summary: A person in India may be liable for helping an act abroad that would be a crime if done in India.

chapterTitle: Of Abetment
title: Punishment of abetment if the act abetted is committed in consequence and where no express provision is made for its punishment
summary: If the encouraged crime happens and no other penalty is specified, the helper may receive the same penalty as for that crime.

chapterTitle: Of Abetment
title: Punishment of abetment if person abetted does act with different intention from that of abettor
summary: If the person helped acts with a different intention, the helper's punishment depends on the intention the helper had.

chapterTitle: Of Abetment
title: Liability of abettor when one act abetted and different act done
summary: A helper may also be responsible for a different act if it was a likely result of the help or plan.

chapterTitle: Of Abetment
title: Abettor when liable to cumulative punishment for act abetted and for act done
summary: If both the planned act and the different act are separate crimes, the helper may be punished for both.

chapterTitle: Of Abetment
title: Liability of abettor for an effect caused by the act abetted different from that intended by the abettor
summary: A helper may be responsible for a different result if they knew that result was likely.

chapterTitle: Of Abetment
title: Abettor present when offence is committed
summary: A helper who is present when the crime occurs may be treated as having committed it.

chapterTitle: Of Abetment
title: Abetment of offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life—if offence not committed
summary: Helping a crime punishable by death or life imprisonment can itself be punished even if the crime does not happen; greater harm can increase the penalty.

chapterTitle: Of Abetment
title: Abetment of offence punishable with imprisonment—if offence be not committed
summary: Helping a crime punishable by imprisonment can be punished even if it does not happen; the penalty can be higher when a responsible public official is involved.

chapterTitle: Of Abetment
title: Abetting commission of offence by the public or by more than ten persons
summary: Encouraging a crime by the public or by more than ten people is punishable.

chapterTitle: Of Abetment
title: Concealing design to commit offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life
summary: Hiding or falsely describing a plan for a crime punishable by death or life imprisonment is punishable, whether or not the crime happens.

chapterTitle: Of Abetment
title: Public servant concealing design to commit offence which it is his duty to prevent
summary: A public official who hides a plan for a crime they must prevent may be punished; the penalty depends on whether the crime occurs.

chapterTitle: Of Abetment
title: Concealing design to commit offence punishable with imprisonment
summary: Hiding or lying about a plan for a crime punishable by imprisonment is punishable, with a higher penalty if the crime happens.

chapterTitle: Criminal Conspiracy (Chapter V-A)
title: Definition of criminal conspiracy
summary: A criminal conspiracy is an agreement by at least two people to commit an illegal act, or to use illegal means for a legal act. In some cases, another step beyond the agreement is required.

chapterTitle: Criminal Conspiracy (Chapter V-A)
title: Punishment of criminal conspiracy
summary: Sets the penalty for joining a criminal conspiracy, an agreement to commit an illegal act. The penalty depends on the seriousness of the planned crime.

chapterTitle: Of Offences Against the State
title: Waging, or attempting to wage war, or abetting waging of war, against the Government of India
summary: Covers waging, or attempting to wage war, or abetting waging of war, against the Government of India.

chapterTitle: Of Offences Against the State
title: Conspiracy to commit offences punishable by section 121
summary: Covers agreeing to wage war against India or to use force to overawe the Central or a State Government. No further act is required for this agreement to be covered.

chapterTitle: Of Offences Against the State
title: Collecting arms, etc., with intention of waging war against the Government of India
summary: Covers collecting arms, and similar conduct, with intention of waging war against the Government of India.

chapterTitle: Of Offences Against the State
title: Concealing with intent to facilitate design to wage war
summary: Covers hiding a plan to wage war against India to help that plan succeed.

chapterTitle: Of Offences Against the State
title: Assaulting President, Governor, etc., with intent to compel or restrain the exercise of any lawful power
summary: Covers assaulting President, Governor, and similar conduct, with intent to compel or restrain the exercise of any lawful power.

chapterTitle: Of Offences Against the State
title: Sedition
summary: Under this source text, sedition covers words, signs, or images that stir or try to stir hatred, contempt, or disloyalty toward the lawful government. It excludes certain lawful criticism.

chapterTitle: Of Offences Against the State
title: Waging war against any Asiatic Power in alliance with the Government of India
summary: Covers waging war against any Asiatic Power in alliance with the Government of India.

chapterTitle: Of Offences Against the State
title: Committing depredation on territories of Power at peace with the Government of India
summary: Covers committing depredation on territories of Power at peace with the Government of India.

chapterTitle: Of Offences Against the State
title: Receiving property taken by war on depredation mentioned in sections 125 and 126
summary: Covers receiving property taken by war on depredation mentioned in sections 125 and 126.

chapterTitle: Of Offences Against the State
title: Public servant voluntarily allowing prisoner of State or war to escape
summary: Covers public official deliberately or knowing the result was likely (intentionally or knowing the result was likely) allowing prisoner of State or war to escape.

chapterTitle: Of Offences Against the State
title: Public servant negligently suffering such prisoner to escape
summary: Covers public official negligently suffering such prisoner to escape.

chapterTitle: Of Offences Against the State
title: Aiding escape of, rescuing or harbouring such prisoner
summary: Covers helping a State prisoner or prisoner of war escape, taking them from custody, hiding them, or resisting their recapture.

chapterTitle: Of Offences relating to the Army, Navy and Air Force
title: Abetting mutiny, or attempting to seduce a soldier, sailor or airman from his duty
summary: Covers helping a mutiny (a rebellion by armed forces), or trying to turn a soldier, sailor, or airman away from their duty.

chapterTitle: Of Offences relating to the Army, Navy and Air Force
title: Abetment of mutiny, if mutiny is committed in consequence thereof
summary: Covers helping or encouraging a crime of mutiny, if mutiny is committed in consequence thereof.

chapterTitle: Of Offences relating to the Army, Navy and Air Force
title: Abetment of assault by soldier, sailor or airman on his superior officer, when in execution of his office
summary: Covers helping or encouraging a crime of assault by soldier, sailor or airman on his superior officer, when in execution of his office.

chapterTitle: Of Offences relating to the Army, Navy and Air Force
title: Abetment of such assault, if the assault is committed
summary: Covers helping or encouraging a crime of such assault, if the assault is committed.

chapterTitle: Of Offences relating to the Army, Navy and Air Force
title: Abetment of desertion of soldier, sailor or airman
summary: Covers helping or encouraging a crime of desertion of soldier, sailor or airman.

chapterTitle: Of Offences relating to the Army, Navy and Air Force
title: Harbouring deserter
summary: Covers hiding or sheltering a soldier, sailor, or airman known to have deserted.

chapterTitle: Of Offences relating to the Army, Navy and Air Force
title: Deserter concealed on board merchant vessel through negligence of master
summary: Covers deserter concealed on board merchant vessel through negligence of master.

chapterTitle: Of Offences relating to the Army, Navy and Air Force
title: Abetment of act of insubordination by soldier, sailor or airman
summary: Covers helping or encouraging a crime of act of insubordination by soldier, sailor or airman.

chapterTitle: Of Offences relating to the Army, Navy and Air Force
title: Application of foregoing sections to the Indian Marine Service
summary: This repealed section covered application of foregoing sections to the Indian Marine Service. The source marks it repealed.

chapterTitle: Of Offences relating to the Army, Navy and Air Force
title: Persons subject to certain Acts
summary: People governed by specified military service laws are generally dealt with under those laws, not this Code, for offences in this chapter.

chapterTitle: Of Offences relating to the Army, Navy and Air Force
title: Wearing garb or carrying token used by soldier, sailor or airman
summary: Covers wearing garb or carrying token used by soldier, sailor or airman.

chapterTitle: Of Offences against the Public Tranquillity
title: Unlawful assembly
summary: An unlawful assembly is a group of five or more people gathered for one of the illegal purposes listed in the Code.

chapterTitle: Of Offences against the Public Tranquillity
title: Being member of unlawful assembly
summary: A person is a member of an unlawful assembly if they knowingly join or remain with the group.

chapterTitle: Of Offences against the Public Tranquillity
title: Punishment
summary: Sets the penalty for being a member of an unlawful assembly.

chapterTitle: Of Offences against the Public Tranquillity
title: Joining unlawful assembly armed with deadly weapon
summary: Sets the penalty for joining an unlawful assembly while carrying a weapon likely to cause death.

chapterTitle: Of Offences against the Public Tranquillity
title: Joining or continuing in unlawful assembly, knowing it has been commanded to disperse
summary: Covers joining or continuing in unlawful assembly, knowing it has been commanded to disperse.

chapterTitle: Of Offences against the Public Tranquillity
title: Rioting
summary: A group commits rioting when it uses force or violence to carry out the unlawful assembly's shared purpose.

chapterTitle: Of Offences against the Public Tranquillity
title: Punishment for rioting
summary: States the possible penalty for rioting.

chapterTitle: Of Offences against the Public Tranquillity
title: Rioting, armed with deadly weapon
summary: Sets the penalty for rioting while armed with a weapon likely to cause death.

chapterTitle: Of Offences against the Public Tranquillity
title: Every member of unlawful assembly guilty of offence committed in prosecution of common object
summary: A person in an unlawful assembly may be held responsible for a crime committed to carry out its shared purpose, or one the members knew was likely.

chapterTitle: Of Offences against the Public Tranquillity
title: Hiring, or conniving at hiring, of persons to join unlawful assembly
summary: Covers hiring, or conniving at hiring, of persons to join unlawful assembly.

chapterTitle: Of Offences against the Public Tranquillity
title: Knowingly joining or continuing in assembly of five or more persons after it has been commanded to disperse
summary: Covers knowingly joining or continuing in assembly of five or more persons after it has been commanded to disperse.

chapterTitle: Of Offences against the Public Tranquillity
title: Assaulting or obstructing public servant when suppressing riot, etc
summary: Covers assaulting or obstructing public official when suppressing riot, and similar conduct

chapterTitle: Of Offences against the Public Tranquillity
title: Wantonly giving provocation with intent to cause riot—if rioting be committed—if not committed
summary: Covers wantonly giving provocation with intent to cause riot—if rioting be committed—if not committed.

chapterTitle: Of Offences against the Public Tranquillity
title: Promoting enmity between different groups on grounds of religion, race, place of birth, residence, language, etc., and doing acts prejudicial to maintenance of harmony
summary: Covers stirring hostility between groups based on religion, race, birthplace, residence, or language, and acts that harm public harmony.

chapterTitle: Of Offences against the Public Tranquillity
title: Punishment for knowingly carrying arms in any procession or organising, or holding or taking part in any mass drill or mass training with arms
summary: States the possible penalty for knowingly carrying arms in any procession or organising, or holding or taking part in any mass drill or mass training with arms.

chapterTitle: Of Offences against the Public Tranquillity
title: Imputations, assertions prejudicial to national-integration
summary: Covers statements or claims that promote hostility toward groups or undermine national unity.

chapterTitle: Of Offences against the Public Tranquillity
title: Owner or occupier of land on which an unlawful assembly is held
